text:
jonathan: Quick RFC follow-up — Private control plane for VPC customers. Two options on the table: 1) customer-facing private endpoint (AWS PrivateLink / GCP Private Service Connect) per-account, or 2) cross-account VPC peering/transit gateway to our central control plane. Thoughts on tradeoffs and long-term maintainability? cc @maya @arvind :thinking_face:

maya: TL;DR: PrivateLink feels cleaner for security and isolation, peering is cheaper at scale but more brittle for multi-region and has route table churn.

arvind: Agree with @maya. A few concrete points: PrivateLink gives us a stable ENI+endpoint model and avoids route propagation issues. But each customer endpoint = AWS endpoint service + NLBs on our side => cost and operational overhead.

lucy: Noted. Also DNS/certs for the control plane endpoint get trickier with PrivateLink because customers expect their internal FQDNs to resolve. We need a plan for delegated zones or customer-managed CNAMEs.

samir: One more angle: Transit Gateway + shared VPC works well for enterprises that want central peering, but it forces cross-account role assumptions and complex RBAC on routing. For SMBs, PrivateLink buys us simpler security posture.

jonathan: Operationally, the biggest concern I have for PrivateLink is request fanout. If we have 200 customers each with endpoints, that's a lot of NLBs + target groups. Can we autoscale control plane stateless services behind fewer NLBs using SNI + TLS routing?

arvind: You can multiplex with ALB/NLB + SNI but PrivateLink requires NLB + static IPs for the service side. We can front many customer endpoints with a single NLB per-region and use target group metadata for routing, but that hurts per-customer isolation.

maya: Proposal: hybrid model for v1 of Private product:
- SMB tier: require PrivateLink (easier for us to isolate and secure)
- Enterprise tier: support Transit Gateway / VPC peering / TGW attachments with optional dedicated control-plane VPCs
This lets us iterate on management automation for endpoints before we take on TGW complexity.

lucy: +1. Also, implement a small DNS operator that creates private hosted zones in the customer's account and injects control-plane records via cross-account role. That solves cert validation and lets customers use internal names.

samir: On long-term refactor: we should separate data-plane and control-plane channels in code and infra. Data-plane (model inferencing) stays customer-VPC local; control-plane can be multiplexed but must provide strong auth (mTLS or signed JWT) and tenant-aware rate-limiting. That gives us freedom to change peering strategy later without touching inference infra.

jonathan: Good call. Action items I hear:
1) Draft a PrivateLink pilot runbook (costs, NLB per-region plan, DNS flow) — @maya
2) Inventory enterprise customers who need TGW/peering and document constraints — @samir
3) Sketch DNS operator and cross-account role flows — @lucy
4) RFC follow-up: add explicit interfaces for control-plane auth (mTLS + token fallback) and data/control separation in the runtime — @arvind
I've created a small checklist in the RFC PR. infra-bot: can you link it?

infra-bot: PR updated: https://git.redwood.internal/rfcs/209-controlplane-privatelink (status: needs-review) :white_check_mark:

maya: I'll start the cost model and a tiny terraform prototype for one endpoint service. Sharing results by EOD Friday.

arvind: I'll take the auth interface sketch and add simple protobuf/gRPC schema for control plane messages so we can proxy without coupling to HTTP.

jonathan: Perfect. Thanks everyone — this follow-up is helpful. We'll reconvene after the prototypes. :thumbsup:
